abstract.para: A &stig; (&stiga;) is a configuration standard that hardens a specific product and version against known threats.

topic.para: The &disa; (&disaa;) approves and publishes &stiga;s. &disaa; is an agency of the United States Department of Defense (DoD). Systems on a DoD network must follow the &stiga; for their product. Other organizations also use &stiga;s as a hardening baseline.

A &stiga; reduces the ways in which a system can be attacked. The rules of a &stiga; limit physical and network access to the system and define maintenance processes, such as applying software updates and patching vulnerabilities. &stiga;s cover operating systems and other components, for example databases, routers and switches.

&disaa; publishes each &stiga; as a checklist for manual review. The &ssg; converts such requirements into Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) content, which &openscap; evaluates automatically. For more information about SCAP and &openscap;, see .
